title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy Presses U.S. Ambassador for H-1B Streamlining and More Student Visas
excerpt: In a 30-minute meeting with Ambassador Sergio Gor, Reddy pushed for faster visa processing, advance notice of regulatory changes, and deeper investment ties between Telangana and the United States.
body:
• Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy met U.S. Ambassador Sergio Gor in New Delhi on August 5 for over 30 minutes to discuss easing H-1B visa processes, increasing student visa slots, and boosting investment ties.
  • Reddy urged streamlined H-1B renewals and stamping procedures and requested advance notice of any regulatory changes affecting Indian professionals in the U.S.
  • The meeting also covered investment opportunities in Telangana's IT, AI, life sciences, and startup sectors, with Gor assuring full cooperation on trade and cultural exchanges.
  • The push comes as Indian professionals face mounting pressure from a proposed $100,000 supplemental H-1B filing fee and a new wage-weighted selection system that replaced the random lottery.

Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy sat down with U.S. Ambassador to India Sergio Gor in New Delhi on Tuesday for a 30-minute meeting that covered the full spectrum of bilateral friction points, from H-1B processing delays to student visa bottlenecks and American investment in Hyderabad's technology corridor.

H-1B and Student Visa Demands

Reddy used the meeting to press for concrete action on visa issues that disproportionately affect Telangana, the state that supplies a substantial share of India's H-1B workforce. He requested that H-1B renewals, stamping procedures, and processing timelines be streamlined to reduce delays that have plagued Indian professionals, according to ANI.

The chief minister also asked the ambassador for more student visa slots for Telangana applicants pursuing higher education in the United States, along with timely visa appointment availability and faster processing of applications.

On regulatory uncertainty, Reddy sought a specific commitment: advance notice of any changes to U.S. visa regulations, a request that reflects widespread anxiety among Indian professionals after a series of abrupt policy shifts under the Trump administration.

A State With Outsized Stakes

Telangana's interest in H-1B policy is not incidental. The Telugu-speaking diaspora from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh reportedly holds approximately 70% of all H-1B visas issued to Indian nationals, according to VisaVerge. Hyderabad's IT corridor, anchored by HITEC City, is a primary feeder of talent to U.S. technology companies.

That concentration makes any change to H-1B rules — including the proposed $100,000 supplemental fee for new petitions filed for workers outside the U.S. and the wage-weighted selection process that replaced the random lottery in February 2026 — a matter of direct economic consequence for the state.

Reddy has been vocal on the issue before. In September 2025, he described the supplemental fee proposal as "totally unacceptable" and called for Prime Minister Narendra Modi and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar to intervene, warning that "the suffering for our Telugu techies will be unimaginable."

Investment Pitch

The visa discussion was paired with an investment push. Reddy highlighted opportunities for American companies in Telangana across IT, artificial intelligence, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, startups, and advanced technologies, according to ANI.

He also proposed expanding university collaborations, student exchange programs, and research initiatives between Telangana institutions and U.S. universities — framing education ties as a two-way channel that benefits both economies.

"Nowhere is the high-speed trajectory of our partnership more evident than in Hyderabad. From HITEC City to aerospace and defence, this region represents progress that is defining our bilateral momentum."

— Sergio Gor, U.S. Ambassador to India

Ambassador Gor, who previously praised Hyderabad's role in U.S.-India ties during the Freedom 250 celebrations in June, assured Reddy of "full cooperation in further strengthening trade, investment, cultural exchanges, and people-to-people ties between Telangana and the United States."

Broader Diplomatic Context

The meeting takes place against a complicated diplomatic backdrop. Gor has publicly maintained that the Trump administration's review of the H-1B program is part of a broader immigration overhaul, not a measure targeting India specifically. At Outlook Business, he said the changes stem from "concerns over immigration management under previous administrations" and align with India's own position on curbing illegal migration.

But the practical impact falls heavily on Indian professionals. Indians received 71% of all approved H-1B visas in 2024, and a projected 40-50% drop in new offshore H-1B petitions — driven by the supplemental fee — could reshape recruitment patterns across the U.S. technology sector.

What's Next

The Telangana Rising 2026 Global Summit in Hyderabad, currently in preparation, aims to attract further foreign investment to the state. Reddy's meeting with Gor serves as a diplomatic prelude to that event, establishing a direct channel between the state government and the U.S. embassy on both economic and immigration issues. Whether the ambassador's assurances translate into concrete policy movement remains to be seen.
